briefs.headline: Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 at Anfield, their first league win there since 2012
briefs.summary: Kai Havertz tapped in at the far post in the 16th minute on Sunday after Alisson's loose pass to Jeremy Jacquet was seized on and worked right through Noni Madueke and Declan Rice. Liverpool had most of the ball after that but never forced David Raya into a save, and a Jurrien Timber tug on Alexander Isak went unpunished by VAR. Havertz's 46th Premier League goal makes him the competition's record German scorer. Arsenal go top on 24 points; Liverpool stay 5th on 15, nine back, and visit Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Steelers run over the Browns 27-6 and take the AFC North lead
briefs.summary: Jaylen Warren ran for 143 yards and a touchdown, Rico Dowdle and Pat Freiermuth also scored on the ground and Pittsburgh sacked Deshaun Watson eight times Sunday at Acrisure Stadium, the Steelers' 23rd straight regular-season home win over Cleveland, tying the NFL record. Watson passed for 324 yards, much of it late; Shedeur Sanders took a few snaps after Watson was shaken up in the first quarter, and the Browns fumbled on consecutive possessions. Jared Verse, who had said it was time to 'make Pittsburgh ours,' finished with one assisted tackle. Cleveland (5-3) visits New Orleans on Sunday.

briefs.headline: Bengals beat the Titans 43-36 in overtime on Burrow's five TD passes and a run
briefs.summary: Joe Burrow hit Tee Higgins for an 18-yard touchdown with 1:17 left to tie it at 36 and scrambled 9 yards untouched in overtime Sunday at Paycor Stadium. He completed 33 of 48 for 462 yards and five scores but threw three interceptions, all to Amari Hooker, and Cincinnati came back from four turnovers and a 13-point first-quarter hole. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase 11 for 141 and a score. The Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since 2021 and play Atlanta in Madrid on Sunday.

briefs.headline: Crew clinch an MLS Cup playoff place as Red Bull New York and Toronto lose
briefs.summary: Columbus clinched a spot in the MLS Cup playoffs on Sunday evening, the club said, when Red Bull New York lost at Nashville and Toronto lost at Atlanta, a day after the Crew's win over D.C. United. Columbus, last in the East in August, sit 8th on 44 points, in a wild-card place, with Red Bull New York (39) out of reach with one match left. Decision Day is Saturday at 4th-place Chicago, 4 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: De Zerbi says Tottenham are 'playing as a team' after a third straight win
briefs.summary: Roberto De Zerbi credited a training trip to Marbella during the October break for the turnaround that has brought three consecutive league wins for the first time in 616 days, ESPN reported Sunday. 'Before the national break we were playing as many very good players, but not as a team,' he said after Saturday's win over 10-man Crystal Palace. He singled out Archie Gray, 20, who scored and has started nine times at right-back this season. Spurs, 8th, visit Leeds on Saturday at 7:30 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Spurs host Utah tonight without Harris and Quaintance; Jazz without Nurkic
briefs.summary: San Antonio, winners of four straight, meet the Jazz, losers of four straight, at the Frost Bank Center at 8:30 p.m. ET Monday, four days after beating them in overtime in Salt Lake City, when Victor Wembanyama scored 36. Tobias Harris (calf) and Jayden Quaintance (knee) are out for the Spurs; Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) are out for Utah. Wembanyama comes off a 43-point game against Minnesota.

briefs.headline: Lamar Jackson needs thumb surgery and goes on IR after Bills rout Ravens 36-10
briefs.summary: Jackson, back from a three-game ankle absence, hit his throwing hand on a Buffalo defender on his first snap Sunday and left in the first quarter; coach Jesse Minter said he will have surgery on the right thumb and go on injured reserve, which keeps him out at least four games. Tyler Huntley left with a toe injury and undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano went 10 of 21 for 91 yards. Baltimore (4-4) plays at Jacksonville on Thursday night.

briefs.headline: Broncos rally past the Chiefs 28-24 to take over first place in the AFC West
briefs.summary: Denver (6-2) erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit Sunday, with Bo Nix throwing two touchdown passes and Jonah Coleman scoring the go-ahead touchdown; Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal and a false start wiped out a final play on which Rashee Rice had come open. Kansas City (5-2) lost its hold on first place in the division. Seattle plays at Chicago tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET to close Week 8.

briefs.headline: Lions end Vikings' unbeaten start 19-15; Campbell carted off with neck injury
briefs.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown and Jameson Williams caught the go-ahead score from Jared Goff on Sunday as Detroit (5-2) handed Minnesota (6-1) its first loss. Linebacker Jack Campbell lay motionless after a fourth-quarter tackle on T.J. Hockenson, was strapped to a backboard and taken to a hospital, where the team said he would stay overnight for evaluation of a neck injury.

briefs.headline: Ohio State drops to No. 11 in AP poll; Utah rises to third, USC returns at 18
briefs.summary: Unbeaten Miami drew 62 of 70 first-place votes in Sunday's poll, with Georgia second and unbeaten Utah up three places to third ahead of Notre Dame and UCLA. Ohio State fell nine spots after its loss at USC, which climbed from unranked to No. 18, and Florida slid from 17th to 25th. New Mexico, with one loss, is ranked for the first time in program history. The College Football Playoff committee issues its first rankings Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Florida State fires Mike Norvell and takes on a buyout of about $47 million
briefs.summary: The school dismissed Norvell on Sunday, a day after Clemson beat Florida State 36-24 in Tallahassee and left the Seminoles with three wins in eight games and one in five in the ACC, the AP reported; he won 41 games and lost 39 in six-plus seasons, and the buyout is 85 percent of his salary through 2031, with assistants' buyouts pushing the total past $50 million. Rick Stockstill, the former Middle Tennessee coach now on FSU's staff, takes over for the last four games.

briefs.headline: Nine first-time winners take Gold Gloves; McLean is the first rookie pitcher
briefs.summary: Rawlings announced the 2026 winners Sunday, with the Red Sox (Caleb Durbin, Wilyer Abreu, Ceddanne Rafaela) and Diamondbacks (Gabriel Moreno, Geraldo Perdomo, Corbin Carroll) taking three each. The Mets' Nolan McLean became the first rookie pitcher to win and the club's first winner at any position since 2014; Cole Young, Ezequiel Duran and Jackson Chourio were among the first-timers. No Reds or Pirates player won.

briefs.headline: Qualifying-offer decisions and open free agency both arrive at 5 p.m. ET today
briefs.summary: Clubs have until 5 p.m. ET to extend the $23.15 million qualifying offer, a record figure, to their departing free agents; Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Trevor Rogers are expected to receive and decline it, and players have until Nov. 17 to decide. The same deadline ends the quiet period, after which Tarik Skubal and the rest of the class can sign anywhere. General managers meet in Las Vegas Nov. 9 to 11, and the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1.

briefs.headline: Hanshin posts Triple Crown winner Teruaki Sato; 45-day window opens today
briefs.summary: Sato, 27, who hit .306 with 39 home runs and 106 RBIs to win the Central League Triple Crown, was made available through the posting system Sunday and can negotiate with all 30 clubs from Monday, MLB.com reported. A third baseman who has also played 262 games in the outfield, he returns to the Tigers for 2027 if no deal is reached within 45 days.

briefs.headline: Lakers hold off the Raptors in Toronto; Warriors beat the Clippers without Curry
briefs.summary: Los Angeles won 131 to 125 in Toronto on Sunday for a fifth win in seven games, and Golden State beat the Clippers 124 to 112 with Stephen Curry and Draymond Green out, dropping Los Angeles' other team to one win in six. Boston beat Orlando 108 to 97 and Brooklyn's 98 to 90 win over Indiana was the Nets' first of the season. Memphis, the league's last unbeaten team at six wins, plays at New Orleans tonight.

briefs.headline: Nashville rally to beat the Red Bulls 3-2 and tie the MLS points record at 74
briefs.summary: Two New York own goals erased a 2-0 deficit and Sam Surridge scored the winner in the 91st minute Sunday at GEODIS Park, where the Supporters' Shield winners finished the regular season 15-0-2 at home, a league record for home wins. Nashville's 74 points equal Inter Miami's 2024 mark; a draw at FC Cincinnati on Decision Day, Saturday at 4 p.m. ET, would make the record theirs alone.

briefs.headline: Vancouver beat Seattle 5-1 to lock up the West's top seed; Portland climbs to 8th
briefs.summary: Brian White scored twice and Ryan Gauld, Mathias Laborda and Aleksa Cvetkovic added goals Sunday at BC Place, giving Vancouver home advantage through the Western Conference final and a club-record 11 home wins. Portland's 3-1 win over Houston, with Vincent Janssen scoring once and setting up two, moved the Timbers from 11th to the last wild-card place and pushed Seattle out; a win at Austin on Saturday clinches a third straight playoff berth for Portland.

briefs.headline: Onosato wins 14 of 20 bouts against Kotozakura as joint practice opens in Fukuoka
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato won 14 of 20 straight bouts against ozeki (champion) Kotozakura on Monday at the Nishonoseki ichimon (stable group) rengo-geiko (joint practice) at Sadogatake stable in Fukuoka, Jiji Press reported; he said he wants to erase last year's memory of withdrawing from the final day with a shoulder injury. Yokozuna Hoshoryu, kyujo (absent) for three straight basho (tournaments) after knee surgery, decides before Friday's bout-scheduling meeting. The Kyushu basho opens Sunday in Fukuoka, six days out.

coming_in.species: Ducks, scaup, mergansers and geese, second segment
coming_in.method: Second segment of a three-way split
coming_in.dates: Oct. 3 to 11, Nov. 7 to 15, Dec. 21 to Jan. 31
coming_in.item: Five days out. The duck table's second segment opens Saturday, Nov. 7, and runs through Nov. 15, with the third Dec. 21 through Jan. 31; the first, Oct. 3 to 11, has closed, and both youth waterfowl days, Sept. 19 and Oct. 31, are past, with no further youth day in the table. The migratory summary's line reads daily bag six, possession 18, with the species sub-limits in its footnote (no more than four mallards, two of them hens, two black ducks, three pintails, three wood ducks, two redheads, two canvasbacks, four sea ducks); scaup, counted inside the duck bag, reads one per day Nov. 7 to 15 and Dec. 21 to Jan. 11 and two per day Jan. 12 to 31; coots run the same dates at 15 and 45, and mergansers the same dates at five and 15 in aggregate; gallinules' second segment is Dec. 2 through Jan. 31. Canada, white-fronted, snow and blue geese share the same Nov. 7 to 15 second segment, with a third Dec. 8 through Jan. 31, at a daily bag of five and possession 15 in aggregate; brant open Jan. 2. Shooting hours for waterfowl are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, identical to Sunday's copy and the same size as every morning since Oct. 17, a 17th straight morning).

coming_in.species: Bobwhite quail, cottontail rabbit, snowshoe hare, ring-necked pheasant, red and gray fox, bobcat, and the furbearer trapping lines
coming_in.method: Hunting and trapping openers of Saturday, Nov. 7
coming_in.item: Five days out. The pamphlet's table opens a run of hunting and trapping lines on Saturday, Nov. 7: bobwhite quail through Jan. 2, daily bag three, possession nine, closed on Tomblin WMA; cottontail rabbit through Feb. 28, daily bag five, possession 20; snowshoe hare through Feb. 28, daily bag two, possession eight; ring-necked pheasant, cock birds only, through Jan. 2, daily bag two, possession two, with a separate Hillcrest WMA line Nov. 14 to Dec. 5 at one, 12 days out; raccoon trapping, and red and gray fox hunting and trapping, through Feb. 28; bobcat hunting and trapping through Feb. 28, season limit three, registration required; and the mink, muskrat, fisher, otter, beaver, skunk, opossum, coyote and weasel trapping lines, fisher and otter at a season limit of one with registration, beaver through March 31. The buck firearms season, Nov. 23 to Dec. 6, is 21 days out, outside two weeks, and the next antlerless deer and gun bear windows, both selected counties with county lists not in the table, open the same day. The pamphlet is valid through June 30, 2027, checked against this morning's date.

prime.method: Second segment of a three-way split
prime.dates: Sept. 1 to Oct. 11, Nov. 2 to 15, Dec. 7 to Jan. 10
prime.item: Day 1, opens today. The second segment of the dove season opens this morning, Monday, Nov. 2, and runs through Nov. 15, 13 days out, with the third Dec. 7 through Jan. 10; the first segment closed Oct. 11. The migratory summary's line reads daily bag 15, possession 45, and its shooting-hours paragraph says dove hours are noon to sunset on opening day of the first segment only and one-half hour before sunrise to sunset during the remainder of the season, so today's opener carries the full hours; its what's-new box says South Branch WMA is no longer under special dove regulations and Stonewall Jackson WMA now is. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes, md5 aad32d21343547146e3977a821a39355, identical to Sunday's copy and the same size as every morning since Oct. 17, a 17th straight morning).

Day 38. Archery and crossbow seasons for deer and for bear opened Sept. 26 and run through Dec. 31 statewide, electronic registration required; limits are on pamphlet pages 13 to 18 for deer and 33 to 39 for bear, vary by county and permit class, and are not in the table, so none is printed. The next antlerless deer and gun bear windows, both selected counties with county lists not in the table, open Nov. 23 alongside the buck firearms season, 21 days out; the table's later antlerless windows are Dec. 10 to 13 and Dec. 28 to 31, and the muzzleloader deer season is Dec. 14 to 20. The pamphlet is valid through June 30, 2027, checked against this morning's date.

prime.item: Day 19. Proclamation SF-1-2026, issued Oct. 2, opened the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters at sunrise Oct. 15, and NCDMF's recreational limits page, read at 5:45 a.m. this morning, says the season runs through March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation, at a 3-inch shell length and one bushel per person per day not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day; the proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:47 a.m., lists no newer shellfish order.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m. (HTTP 200, 108,142 bytes, the same size as Thursday through Sunday), lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, with the notes that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches and unlawful to gig, spear or gaff them. The page's footer still reads that the document is effective Nov. 1, 2026, yesterday; every line this paper prints was compared against Sunday's reading and none has changed, so the second morning on the new effective date brings no change this paper can find to red drum, seatrout, flounder, the mackerels, bluefish, black drum, sheepshead, spot, croaker or oysters, though the server's Last-Modified header now reads 10:41 GMT today on a cache miss, where Sunday's read Oct. 31, and Sunday's saved copy did not survive for a byte diff, so the comparison is line by line, not byte by byte; today's copy is saved for tomorrow's. The proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:47 a.m., still ends at the two orders issued Friday, Oct. 30, FF-49-2026 and FF-50-2026, both commercial closures (Atlantic croaker from Dec. 16 and spot from Jan. 1, 2027); nothing dated Oct. 31, Nov. 1 or today appears on it, and nothing recreational has been issued since the Oct. 27 gill net order M-25-2026.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m., lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, unchanged from Sunday on the page's Nov. 1 effective date; the proclamations index read at 5:47 a.m. carries no seatrout proclamation since the July 1 harvest opening, FF-31-2026. The reference calendar lists speckled trout as prime in November, and the Fisherman's Post November report, published Sunday, says the piers have started seeing scattered speckled trout and the guides are finding them in the creeks; Beaufort's thermometer, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.6F at 5:30 a.m., down from 65.7F Sunday.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m., lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day, up to seven per person on a for-hire vessel, all unchanged from Sunday on the page's Nov. 1 effective date. Nothing on the three has been issued by proclamation since October began, and the index read at 5:47 a.m. carries nothing dated since Oct. 30.

prime.species: Black drum, sheepshead, spot and croaker
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning at 5:45 a.m., lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day with one over 25 inches allowed, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, spot with no minimum size and 50 per day, and Atlantic croaker with no minimum size and 50 per day, all unchanged from Sunday on the page's Nov. 1 effective date. The two newest orders on the index, read at 5:47 a.m., are both commercial: FF-49-2026, issued Oct. 30, closes the commercial croaker fishery from Dec. 16, and FF-50-2026, issued Oct. 30 and effective Jan. 1, 2027, closes the commercial spot fishery; neither touches the recreational line. The reference calendar lists spot and black drum running into November.

waters.reading: 61.5 cfs, 1.39 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and steady on stage against 71.4 cfs and 1.46 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Down 4.1 cfs and 0.03 feet on the day against the USGS trace's 65.6 cfs and 1.42 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, Sunday's edition reading, a 16th straight falling morning and the smallest drop of the recession: 103 Tuesday, 94 Wednesday, 85 Thursday, 79 Friday, 73 Saturday, 66 Sunday, 62 Monday, drops of 9, 8, 6, 6, 7 and 4. The trace is the same stair-step with no rain bump, 65.6 through mid-morning Sunday, flickering between 65.6 and 64.2 from about 10:30 a.m., 64.2 from about 12:45 p.m., 62.8 from about 8:30 p.m. and 61.5 from 4:45 a.m., the stage sliding 1.42 to 1.39 behind it. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, printed as it stands, "62 cfs - prime wading water.", and its 71.4 cfs and 1.46 feet comparison points are Saturday values on the trace, not Sunday's, so the 9.9-cfs drop they imply is two days' worth; the falling flag on discharge is right in direction, and the steady flag on stage is the fetcher's band verdict on a 0.07-foot change. The river's most recent stocking this paper has reported is Thursday, Oct. 29, from WVNS's Oct. 29 list; no list dated Oct. 31, Nov. 1 or today could be found this morning, so Thursday's fish have had four nights to spread out of the first pools below the truck stops. At 62 cfs and clear on the second morning of November the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure hold less water than on any morning of this 16-day recession; the wading is easy everywhere, the fish are pinned to what current is left, the heads and tongues of the plunge pools, the single deep slot in each run of pocket water and the shade under the cut banks, and at this clarity they see a wader from a long way off. This is a long-leader, small-fly problem, as it was Sunday: a 12-foot leader to 6X or 7X, a size 20 to 22 blue-winged olive or a small parachute Adams on top through the middle of the day, when the light and the air are warmest, a size 18 or 20 pheasant tail or zebra midge dropped 18 inches under it through the morning for the caddis and small stonefly nymphs the file records as forage, and a size 10 olive sculpin pattern or a small black woolly bugger swung slow and deep through the plunge pools at dusk, the one heavier fly the low water still allows and one the stocked fish take too; an egg pattern or a bright San Juan worm under a small indicator covers the holdover stocked pools without changing the rig. Drab clothing, a low approach from below at the pool tails and the first cast count for more than the pattern at this flow.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.79 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.78 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.8 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool steady, a hundredth over its 24.78 comparison point, but that point is not the trace's 5 a.m. Sunday value, which was 24.61, Sunday's edition reading; against that the gauge is up 0.18 on the day, still inside the quarter-foot band the fetcher calls steady, so the flag stands and the pool above Byrd has turned from easing to filling. The trace shows the pool draining through Sunday morning, 24.61 at 4:45 a.m., 24.53 at 6 a.m., 24.41 at 8 a.m., a 24.31 low at about 2 p.m., then climbing from late afternoon, 24.53 at 5 p.m., 24.55 at 8:30, 24.61 at 10 p.m., 24.65 at 11:45 p.m., 24.73 at 2:15 a.m. and 24.79 at 5 a.m., the morning's high. Nothing upstream is feeding it that the gauges show: the Williams is falling, and the Huntington airport's only weather in its overnight observations through 5:15 a.m. is light rain at 3:20 a.m. this morning with no measurable amount recorded. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.8 the gauge is 2.2 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. A pool sitting at normal and filling slowly fishes the structure, not the slack: shad are the forage and the skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap at first light for the hybrids and white bass pushing bait against the rock, a crawfish-colored jig or a three-inch tube dragged slow on the riprap for smallmouth and drum once the sun is on the water, and, with the river cooling into November, a half-ounce blade bait or a jig and minnow worked vertical along the lock wall's seam and the edges of the barge cuts, where the sauger stack as the water cools; cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts after dark for blue catfish. The slack behind the dams is for when the river colours, and the trace shows no colour coming.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.77 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 25.7 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.8 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge steady, up 0.07 on its 25.7 comparison point, but that point is not the trace's 5 a.m. Sunday value, which was 26.59, Sunday's edition reading; against that the gauge is down 0.82 on the day, the whole of Saturday's rise given back and more, and the steady flag is wrong in direction for the day even if it is right for the overnight. The weekend's pool transfer reversed on Sunday. The trace peaked at 26.63 at 4:45 a.m. Sunday, held 26.60 at 5:45, then fell all day with hardly a pause: 26.44 at 6:45 a.m., 26.32 at 9:45, 26.00 at 11:45, 25.82 at 3:45 p.m., 25.62 at 7:45, a 25.55 low at 8:15 p.m., and then a flat overnight between 25.58 and 25.79, 25.77 at 5 a.m., 1.23 feet under the 27-foot line between normal pool and up and pushing that Sunday's peak stopped 0.37 short of. The water went on down the river: the USGS gauge on the Ohio at Ironton, Ohio, below Greenup Dam, the next dam down, recorded Greenup's discharge at 39,700 cfs at 5 a.m. Sunday, a 41,000 peak at 11 a.m., 22,400 by 5 p.m., 7,790 by 9:30 p.m. and 3,860 at 5 a.m. today, so Greenup passed on Sunday what Byrd had passed down Saturday night, and with the pool above Byrd at Point Pleasant up 0.18 on the same day, less is now coming through Byrd than on Saturday. Whether that is a scheduled pool adjustment or a lockage pattern, the traces do not say, and this paper will not guess; the only rain in the airport's overnight record is light rain at Huntington at 3:20 a.m. today with no measurable amount. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Falling, clear water below the dam softens the seams Sunday's push had sharpened: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon down the current face of each wing dam, with the eddy behind each one now holding less bait than on Sunday's harder flow, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the lock wall's seam for the sauger, which hold on the wall's downstream edge whatever the dam is passing, a crawfish jig on the riprap, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the slack beside the dam's discharge for blue and flathead catfish after dark, with less current moving the bait to them than on Sunday.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 1:43 AM at 3.5 ft, low 8:11 AM at 0.4 ft, high 2:17 PM at 4.2 ft, low 9:07 PM at 0.6 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 12:55 AM at 4.0 ft, low 6:50 AM at 0.6 ft, high 1:27 PM at 5.0 ft, low 7:55 PM at 0.6 ft. Water 64.6F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon last quarter, 51% lit, 22.1 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 1:43 AM and 2:17 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Last quarter: the fetcher's file carries the moon at 51 percent lit and 22.1 days old, and the tides are at neap, the gentlest of the month, with the sound's afternoon high at 4.2 feet against Sunday's 4.3, Saturday's 4.5 and Friday's 4.6 and the surf high at 5.0 against 5.2, 5.5 and 5.9, so the inlet runs easier than it has in a week and less bait moves on each change. All four of the sound's events at Hampstead land inside today, and all four of the surf's do too: a 3.5-foot high at 1:43 a.m., a drain to a 0.4-foot low at 8:11 a.m., about two and a quarter hours after press time, a fill of 3.8 feet to the 4.2-foot high at 2:17 p.m., and a drain of 3.6 feet to a 0.6-foot low at 9:07 p.m. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 12:55 a.m. at 4.0, low 6:50 a.m. at 0.6, high 1:27 p.m. at 5.0, low 7:55 p.m. at 0.6, so the sound lags the surf by 48 and 50 minutes on the highs and 81 and 72 minutes on the lows, the long-lag-on-the-ebb pattern the reference describes, shorter on both counts at neap. Beaufort's thermometer, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.6F at 5:30 a.m., down 1.1 on the day and 3.2 since Saturday. What's running comes, after eight mornings in fallback, from a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail/Sneads Ferry November report, published Sunday, Nov. 1, at 8 a.m. Eastern, 22 hours old this morning and inside the 21-day gate; it is a monthly report and describes the fishing of the past week or two, not today's water. The Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout starting to show, bottom fishing better at night with good-sized Virginia mullet and spot, and bluefish thick in the early mornings; the Surf City Pier reports pompano, black drum and croakers on the bottom, casting shots at Spanish mackerel and bluefish, and king mackerel fishing that was "really good before this last blow". East Coast Sports has the piers taking a few big red drum over 32 inches at the north end of the island, kings off the piers in double digits a day before the wind, and smaller reds with the odd speckled trout in the sound; Native Son has trout in the creeks on 5- to 8-foot seams, reds on inside waters on artificials with cut bait likely to do best, and Spanish, bluefish and false albacore off the beach; Speckled Specialist is finding numbers of smaller trout to 28 inches, black drum to 18 and smaller reds in 4 to 16 feet of water, most in 4 to 8, on live shrimp under a cork and 3/16-ounce jigheads with soft plastics such as a Slick Jr.; Carolina Flats is scouting trout schools early on topwater and working reds on the oyster and grass banks with soft plastics, Gulp named. That squares with the reference calendar's November pattern, speckled trout prime with red drum, bluefish, spot and sea mullet. Tide is the whole game here, and with the water cooling the report's trout are the fish on the structure the file records: a popping cork with live shrimp over the oyster bars on the first of the flood behind the 8:11 a.m. low and again on the last of the ebb toward 9:07 p.m., a 3/16- or quarter-ounce jighead with a paddletail or a soft jerkbait worked slow along the grass edges and the 5- to 8-foot drop into the ICWW channel on either side of the 2:17 p.m. high, and the same plastics or a suspending twitchbait under the dock lights after dark, where the finger mullet, shrimp and mud minnows stack up on the evening ebb. Red drum want the last of the fall, which today runs from 2:17 to 9:07 p.m., so cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce jighead fan-cast a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges as the grass drains from about 6:30 p.m., well after dark, to the 9:07 p.m. low, with the top of the flood around 2:17 p.m. the second look at drum on the flooded grass and oyster banks, a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic worked over the edges. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel an hour either side of the 2:17 p.m. high, and the piers' night bottom bite says the same rig works after dark. Bluefish are a metal jig or a topwater plug behind the bait pods on the beach in the early morning, the piers' and the report's best window for them, and with the advisory gone the beach is open water again. NWS Wilmington, read at 5:45 a.m.: no alert is active for Coastal Pender or Coastal Onslow, and the coastal-waters zones from Surf City to Cape Fear and Cape Fear to Little River Inlet (AMZ252 and AMZ254) list none either, so the Small Craft Advisory that was to end at 3 a.m. today is off the board.
waters.source: NOAA CO-OPS 8657813 (sound), 8657419 (surf); NWS Wilmington; Fisherman's Post, Topsail/Sneads Ferry November 2026, published Nov. 1
